title: Have and have not
description: Say what you have, had and do not have - belongings, family, time, and aches and colds.

guide.title: 'Mine there is': possessive + আছে
guide.text:
Bengali has no verb 'to have'. Instead of 'I have a car' you say 'my a car exists': আমার একটা গাড়ি আছে।

The owner is in the possessive (আমার, আপনার, ওর, রাজের). The verb আছে agrees with the thing owned, not with the owner, so it is nearly always আছে: আমার ... আছে, আপনার ... আছে, ওদের ... আছে.

The one exception is when what you 'have' is a person who deserves respect: আমার একজন দাদা আছেন, 'I have an elder brother'.

A question needs only a rising tone or কি: আপনার ছেলেমেয়ে আছে? 'Do you have children?'

guide.title: Have not: নেই
guide.text:
The negative of আছে is নেই (nei), for every person: আমার গাড়ি নেই, 'I don't have a car'; আমার সময় নেই, 'I have no time'.

Never say আছে না.

In the negative the noun usually drops একটা: 'I don't have a car' is simply আমার গাড়ি নেই.

examples.english: I don't have time right now.

guide.title: Have it on you: কাছে
guide.text:
For things you are carrying or have available right now - money, a pen, change, a ticket - Bengali says 'near me': আমার কাছে ... আছে.

আমার কাছে টাকা নেই - I have no money on me.
আমার টাকা নেই - I have no money (I am poor).

আপনার কাছে খুচরো আছে? - Do you have change (on you)?

examples.english: I have no money on me.

guide.title: Had, will have
guide.text:
আছে exists only in the present. Its past is ছিল (chhilo): আমার একটা কুকুর ছিল, 'I had a dog'. Negative: ছিল না.

For the future, থাকা (to stay) steps in: কাল আমার সময় থাকবে, 'I will have time tomorrow'; থাকবে না, 'won't have'.

examples.english: We didn't have a TV then.

guide.title: Having a fever, a cold, hunger
guide.text:
Illnesses and bodily feelings are not 'had' with আছে. They 'happen to', 'strike' or 'catch' you, and you are again in the possessive.

হয়েছে (has happened): আমার জ্বর হয়েছে, 'I have a fever'; সর্দি হয়েছে, 'have a cold in the nose'.
লেগেছে (has struck): আমার ঠান্ডা লেগেছে, 'I have caught a cold'.
ধরেছে (has caught): আমার মাথা ধরেছে, 'I have a headache'.
পেয়েছে (has got): আমার খিদে পেয়েছে, 'I am hungry'; তেষ্টা পেয়েছে, 'am thirsty'; ঘুম পেয়েছে, 'am sleepy'.

phrases.note: ছেলেমেয়ে, 'boys-girls', is the usual word for one's children.
শ before ন is a true s: pros-no.

phrases.english: I have no money on me.

phrases.note: Called out at a door. The polite ending is used because you do not know who will answer.

phrases.english: We didn't have a TV then.
